corrections.evidence: Heavy 8-batch probe rerun 2026-05-13 (see _audit_tmp/oleys-waf-r2.out): cf-ray on every batch but no x-sucuri-*, no x-iinfo, no incap_ses, no Reblaze. BATCH 2 (4 UAs): all 200, identical bytes. BATCH 3 (10 rapid bursts): all 200, no rate-limit. BATCH 4 (honeypots): wp-admin/wp-login/.env/.git 403 with body size 552 bytes = BC origin default 403 page, NOT a CDN challenge body. xmlrpc/phpinfo return 404 with BC's 207KB homepage. BATCHES 5-8 (suspicious UA / SQLi / XSS / no-UA): all 200. Interpretation guide: 'cf-ray header present but all 200 -> wafType: cloudflare-passive' — skill operational rule says cloudflare-passive maps to runtime hasWaf=false. DB JSON's wafType: 'cloudflare-passive' is internally inconsistent with DB column hasWaf: true.
corrections.operationalImpact: DB column hasWaf:true causes catalog-crawler to apply WAF-mode pacing (slower perPage, longer delays). Site has no active WAF blocking and can crawl at perPage=100 normally. Recommendation: flip DB column to false when promoting R2.

skillHarnessGaps.gap: Skill's Rule-C wording allows AI to drop catalogUrls based on 'pure apparel' interpretation
skillHarnessGaps.impact: R1 dropped /swag/ citing 'pure apparel — exclude' but Rule C says NEVER drop without walk-proof of zero unique contribution. /swag/ contributes 64 unique products with no overlap. R1 violated Rule C by applying a scope-judgment that contradicts the Rule.
skillHarnessGaps.fix: Strengthen Rule C: 'NEVER drop a catalogUrl based on category name or product type. The only valid reason to drop is: walked product URLs are 100% subset of the union of other walked catalogUrls (i.e. zero unique contribution). Scope judgments (apparel-only, accessories-only) MAY NOT override this rule.'
